RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 55

An all-male panel is not evidence on its own — plenty of such panels pick the better candidate. Treat it as context, not your argument. Some jurisdictions do require gender balance on selection committees, so check whether the composition itself breached a rule; if so, that's a procedural point worth naming.

Lead instead with the substance: you hold a master's in educational leadership and five years actually doing the job; he has "courses" and classroom years. That comparison, not the panel's sex, is what makes the outcome look questionable.

Lead with the unanswered request. Failure to give written reasons within a reasonable period is usually a breach in itself. Send a dated follow-up, keep records, then decide about a formal complaint.
